home

The home land loss series gives home two neighbours that put pressure on the word. What belongs to a place, what belongs to the person who remembers it, and what travels when they leave? The domestic spaces of a humid home full of light and boundary conditions raise a related question about familiarity. A place can become home through acts repeated until they feel ordinary. How much of that life can be revisited in an image after either the place or the person has changed? Home · boundary conditions

Reading note. Absurdism. In The Myth of Sisyphus, Albert Camus associates the feeling of the absurd with becoming a stranger in a world that had seemed familiar. The home land loss works give that estrangement somewhere concrete to begin. What makes a setting feel like home, and how much of that feeling can an image bring back? The Myth of Sisyphus, “Absurdity and Suicide”
